hasPart.name: Diagnosing DHCP address pool exhaustion
hasPart.text: A server needs an available address in the selected pool to allocate a fresh lease to a new, unreserved client. Existing clients can remain online using valid leases after the pool fills. To distinguish exhaustion from a relay problem, check that the server received the client’s discovery and inspect availability in the pool selected for that subnet.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing an incorrect default gateway
hasPart.text: For an off-link destination with no more specific host route, an IPv4 host sends the frame to its configured default gateway. It can still reach on-link peers when that gateway setting is wrong. Compare the configured next hop with the network plan, then test the intended router interface before investigating its upstream routes.

hasPart.name: Identifying an incorrect IPv4 address
hasPart.text: A syntactically valid IPv4 address can belong to a different subnet from the one assigned to the interface. Check the host address and mask against the documented prefix for its VLAN. The address source helps distinguish a static entry error from an unexpected dynamic assignment.

citation.name: RFC 4363 §5, dot1qPvid and VLAN classification of untagged frames

hasPart.name: Confirming a duplicate IPv4 address
hasPart.text: On an ordinary single LAN, an ARP packet claiming a host’s own IPv4 address from another device’s MAC address is evidence of a conflict. A host detecting a conflict can defend or relinquish the address. Identify both claimants before correcting the allocation. A single unanswered ping does not establish a duplicate.

citation.name: RFC 5227 §2.4, Ongoing Address Conflict Detection and Address Defense

hasPart.name: Diagnosing an incorrect subnet mask
hasPart.text: For example, 192.0.2.10/24 treats 192.0.2.140 as on-link. If the intended prefix is 192.0.2.0/25 and the destination is on another Ethernet segment, that host can issue unanswered ARP requests for the destination. A host configured with too narrow a prefix can instead send traffic for an intended local peer to its gateway.
